item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a 2024 source showing Tinubu personally ordered a nationwide internet shutdown or a new mass-surveillance program. The clearest pattern is narrower and more common in Nigeria’s recent record: legal/administrative pressure on journalists, traffic-centralization rules, platform blocking, and cybercrime enforcement.","evidence":[{"title":"Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The report says there were no restrictions on connectivity to the internet or mobile networks during the coverage period, which is the main positive sign on this lens. It also notes that internet freedom still declined because of legal pressure and intimidation, so this is only weak evidence against shutdown-style repression.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigeria, U.S. Agree to Harness Artificial Intelligence, Facilitate Data Flows and Empower Digital Upskilling; Issue Joint Statement","publisher":"Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy","date":"July 27, 2024","url":"https://fmcide.gov.ng/u-s-nigeria-reach-agreement-to-harness-artificial-intelligence-facilitate-data-flows-and-empower-digital-upskilling-issue-joint-statement/","summary":"Nigeria publicly committed to “open, interoperable, reliable and secure Internet” language, plus cross-border data flows and digital upskilling. This is the best positive evidence that Tinubu’s administration was not oriented toward blanket digital closure.","question_ids":["4B.9"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The report says February 2024 amendments to the Cybercrimes Act require public and private organizations to route traffic through SOCs and a national CERT, and that the May 2024 directive called for full implementation. That is strong evidence for a centralized digital-control architecture that could facilitate surveillance or restrictions.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The same report says the Inspector General of Police told the National Cybercrime Center to monitor and prosecute people spreading “false information” and cyberbullying. That is direct evidence of administrative surveillance / prosecution pressure on online speech.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024","summary":"The report also says the government ordered telecoms to block cryptocurrency trading sites in February 2024 and that some political websites remained inaccessible. Even if the crypto order was not primarily political, it shows the state was willing to use digital blocking powers.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigeria has detained a journalist who reported on corruption in a widening crackdown","publisher":"Reuters via GPB","date":"May 9, 2024","url":"https://www.gpb.org/news/2024/05/09/nigeria-has-detained-journalist-who-reported-on-corruption-in-widening-crackdown","summary":"Reuters reported journalist Daniel Ojukwu was held by police under the Cybercrime Act after a corruption investigation, with the outlet and rights groups describing it as intimidation of independent journalism. This is strong negative evidence for administrative harassment using digital law.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigerian police secretly arrest journalist Daniel Ojukwu over critical report","publisher":"Committee to Protect Journalists","date":"May 8, 2024","url":"https://cpj.org/2024/05/nigerian-police-secretly-arrest-journalist-daniel-ojukwu-over-critical-report/","summary":"CPJ says Ojukwu went missing, was held in police custody, and was accused of violating the Cybercrimes Act after reporting on public spending. This is direct evidence of the state using cybercrime enforcement to suppress critical reporting.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"4 Nigerian journalists charged with cybercrime, defamation over fraud investigation","publisher":"Committee to Protect Journalists","date":"February 9, 2024","url":"https://cpj.org/2024/02/4-nigerian-journalists-charged-with-cybercrime-defamation-over-fraud-investigation/","summary":"CPJ reports that four journalists were arrested after reporting on corruption at Kwara State Polytechnic. This is another concrete case of online/journalistic harassment through criminal process.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting","publisher":"Committee to Protect Journalists","date":"October 3, 2024","url":"https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/","summary":"CPJ reported that four more journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite the February reform. That undercuts any claim that Tinubu’s government had moved away from digital-law harassment.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6"]},{"title":"Nigeria: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says officials publicly criticize, harass, and arrest journalists, especially over corruption and sensitive political issues. That is broader context supporting the negative side: the administration tolerated a coercive information environment even if it did not impose a nationwide shutdown.","question_ids":["4B.9","4B.6","4B.7"]}]}
